# Split, on evidence rather than on taste

The solution record for the whole of SEEN-089 scored 0.50, 0.51 and 0.49 on `solution_complete`, and
closing four genuine gaps in it moved the score by 0.01. The same question, asked about the RED rule
alone, scored 0.67. Seven enforcements in one five-point ticket cannot be described in a record
anyone can judge complete, and the model was consistent about it across seven attempts.

Decision by the founder, 23 September 2026: SEEN-089 keeps the TDD enforcement, which is the RED
rule, the coverage gate on `packages/core` and the refusal-message fix. SEEN-094 takes delivery and
merge verification: CI green on the commit the receipt attests, `harness verify-merge`, the pull
request template with the receipt hash, and gitleaks plus `pnpm audit` in CI. Both escaped-defect
fixes travel together in SEEN-094, which keeps them one story.

The backlog is now 94 tickets and 329 build points; Sprint 0 carries 23 tickets and 73 points. Two
things changed the total today: SEEN-093, which added `reopen`, and this split.
